articles.title: EMIB vs. CoWoS: Google, Amazon Back Intel for Inference as Nvidia Keeps Training on TSMC
articles.description: Intel EMIB vs TSMC CoWoS: Google, Amazon, and Cisco have committed to Intel’s EMIB-T advanced packaging for inference-class AI chips, creating the first workload-structured packaging duopoly in AI silicon while Nvidia’s training GPUs remain on TSMC CoWoS. A geometric cost advantage compounding with
articles.content: A fresh analysis from ZDNet Korea, published September 11, 2026, documents a split that has been quietly forming for two years in the AI chip supply chain: the world's largest AI accelerators are no l... [20527 symbols]
articles.summary: The world's largest AI accelerators are no longer using the same packaging technology as TSMC's CoWoS. While Nvidia's flagship training processors continue to rely on CoWOS, Google, Amazon, Cisco, SpaceX, and Tesla have all committed to Intel's Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge (EMIB) for their inference-class chips and custom AI processors. EMIB, which embeds small silicon bridges directly into the organic package substrate, aligns with the needs of these chips at lower package sizes. This eliminates assembly complexity and removes the primary cost driver: the full silicon interposer in CoWos represents 40 to 60 percent package cost, which Intel claims produces a reduction reduction of 50 percent at equivalent package size. The current round-wafer geometry sets a large limit on how large packages can grow efficiently.
articles.shortSummary: The world's largest AI accelerators are shifting focus to Intel's EMIB technology over CoWoS's CoWOS, driven by workload demands and increasing production costs.

articles.title: TSMC Opens Kaohsiung Supplier Campus to Close Packaging Validation Gap
articles.description: TSMC advanced packaging supplier campus in Kaohsiung’s Baipu Industrial Park will co-locate materials suppliers alongside TSMC engineers in shared cleanrooms, boosting CoWoS packaging validation efficiency by 25-50% and accelerating the AI chip supply chain ramp at Chiayi, Longtan, and Tongluo
articles.content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. on Tuesday revealed that it is establishing a dedicated materials and equipment supplier campus inside Kaohsiung's Baipu Industrial Park — a facility designed no... [14563 symbols]
articles.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) has opened a dedicated materials and equipment supplier campus in Kaohsiung's Baipu Industrial Park, designed to reduce the time it takes to qualify the next generation of materials needed to build AI chips. The campus will be the first in Taiwan specifically dedicated to co-locating advanced packaging materials and technology suppliers alongside TSMC's own engineers, and is expected to improve packaging validation efficiency by 25 to 50 percent. The site will include two buildings with modular cleanroom facilities designed for reconfiguration as packaging technologies evolve. Small laboratories will serve as joint testing and R&D spaces for TSMC and its packaging materials, and a dedicated training center for advanced packaging specialists. The goal is to build a world-class packaging talent base while connecting local suppliers directly with global supply chains.
articles.shortSummary: TSMC is establishing a dedicated materials and equipment campus in Kaohsiung to reduce packaging validation time, enhancing AI chip production efficiency by up to 50%.

articles.summary: Imec's commercial chip services division, IC-Link, joined the TSMC 3DFabric Alliance in May, giving fabless design teams a verified co-design pathway into TSMC's CoWoS and SoIC advanced packaging technologies. The partnership is highlighted at the 2026 TSMC North America OIP Forum in Santa Clara. IC-link is the commercial ASIC and silicon photonics arm of imec, one of the world's leading nanoelectronics research institutes. The 3DFaric Alliance membership makes IC-L the first European-headquartered ASIC partner to carry all three TSMC OIP memberships simultaneously, allowing it to handle the full scope of an advanced-node chiplet design under one engagement.
articles.shortSummary: IC-Link joined the TSMC 3DFabric Alliance, providing IC-Link with verified CoWoS and SoIC packaging technology for advanced chip designs, enhancing multi-die multi-system integration.

articles.description: TSMC Q2 2026 earnings on July 16 will reveal whether the AI infrastructure buildout is still accelerating, with investors focused on three signals: full-year revenue guidance, CoWoS advanced packaging capacity in the AI chip supply chain, and whether the company revises its capital expenditure
articles.content: A typhoon that shut down Taiwan's financial markets on Friday forced TSMC to postpone its June 2026 monthly sales data release — a routine disclosure that investors had been counting on as their last ... [19883 symbols]
articles.summary: TSMC's second-quarter 2026 earnings will be released before U.S. markets open on July 16, following a typhoon that shut down Taiwan's financial markets forced the postponement of its June 2026 monthly sales data release. The company's Q2 2026 results are expected to be followed by a conference call at 2:00 a.m. ET (2:00 GMT) at the Mandarin Oriental in Taipei. Wall Street expects Q2 revenue of roughly $40 billion, compared to $30.07 billion in Q2 2025, a year-over-year increase of about 33%. Analysts estimate Q2 earnings per ADR unit at approximately $3.80-$3.83, up from $2.47 a year ago. However, the revenue figure is not the only company that can answer this question: whether the AI infrastructure buildout is decelerating or accelerating. The answer will affect Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, and other semiconductor-adjacent positions in the market. The full-year 2026 revenue growth forecast on the Q1 2026 is expected to exceed 30% in dollar terms, driven by strong demand for advanced AI chips and higher wafer revenue. If TSMC raises its guidance on Q2 2020, it will signal an increase in price increases, indicating that the industry's future in the industry has an explicit runway for the AI capex cycle.
articles.shortSummary: TSMC's Q2 earnings, delayed due to a typhoon, testifies the company's position as an important supplier for AI infrastructure spending and pricing increases.

articles.content: Taiwan's most watched domestic semiconductor land deal is back on track. After residents of Longtan, a district in Taoyuan in northern Taiwan, reversed their opposition to the area's third-phase scien... [16241 symbols]
articles.summary: TSMC is reviving its bid to build two to three next-generation 1.4nm fabrication plants and two advanced packaging facilities at Longtan, a district in Taoyuan in northern Taiwan. This move comes after residents of Longtan reversed their opposition to the area's third-phase science park expansion. The five-facility plan would create what analysts describe as the densest concentration of cutting-edge semiconductor capacity Taiwan has built since the original Hsinchu Science Park cluster decades ago. However, there are still significant hurdles to the site, including an ongoing Executive Yuan review and an environmental impact assessment yet to clear, and land acquisition from predominantly private landowners will not be completed until 2029.
articles.shortSummary: TSMC is resurrecting Longtan's third-phase science park expansion with plans to build two to three next-generation 1.4nm fabrication plants alongside two advanced packaging facilities.

articles.content: Microsoft is negotiating with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. to lock in production capacity for more than 300,000 units of its next-generation Maia 300 AI accelerator, with delivery targeted f... [14627 symbols]
articles.summary: Microsoft is negotiating with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) to secure production capacity for over 300,000 units of its next-generation Maia 300 AI accelerator, with delivery set for 2027 and a public reveal planned as soon as September. However, the challenge is that every AI accelerator depends on a single packaging process controlled exclusively by TSMC, which is already dominated by Nvidia. The CoWoS, a 2.5D packaging technology developed by TSM, is the single global supply constraint on the AI accelerator market. Nvidia alone holds roughly 60 percent of TSMC's CoWSO allocation, with the top three customers accounting for more than 85 percent of total capacity. Despite doubling CoWOS capacity annually since 2023, demand has consistently outrun this expansion.
articles.shortSummary: Microsoft is negotiating with TSMC to secure 300,000 units of CoWoS packaging for its next-generation AI accelerator, aiming for production in 2027 despite current supply constraints.

articles.content: The name said everything. When engineers at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. began work on a new advanced chip-packaging technology, they reached for a competitor's vocabulary to describe it. Th... [18744 symbols]

articles.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) is developing a new advanced chip-packaging technology, "EMIB-like" project, inspired by Intel's Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge (EMIB), in partnership with Kinsus Interconnect Technology Corp. The project is referred to internally as "EMib-like," borrowing the acronym of Intel's EMIB-like approach to assembling complex AI chips. The news of this development led to a 7% increase in TSMC's shares and a 13% increase for Intel's, suggesting that the AI packaging race is large enough for both companies to gain simultaneously. However, TSMC CEO C.C. Wei acknowledged the difficulty of TSMC’s tight packaging capacity, stating that it limits its customers’ growth. CoWoS-S, the first-generation platform for AI chips, uses a full monolithic silicon interposer across the entire package and supports packages of roughly 333 times the current reticle limit. The future of CoWOS-S is set to support packages of approximately 35,000 CoWOs wafer starts per month in late 2024 to a projected 130,000 by year-end 2026, a near fourfold increase.
articles.shortSummary: TSMC is developing "EMIB-like" chip packaging technology with Kinsus to compete with Intel's multi-die Interconnect Bridge, addressing a physical and market bottleneck affecting AI chip production.

articles.summary: Foxconn CEO Michael Chiang has named CoWoS Packaging as the 2027 AI Server Ceiling after record Q2 earnings for the first time in the company's history, earning more from AI servers than from iPhones and other consumer electronics combined. The Taiwanese manufacturer, Hon Hai Precision Industry, reported a net profit of NT$59.97 billion (approximately $1.86 billion), a 35% year-on-year increase from the NT$44.4 billion the previous year. Foxconn's cloud-and-networking segment accounted for 51% of Q2 2026 total revenue, a significant increase from 48% in Q1 2026. The company's operating profit hit an all-time quarterly record of NT $94.8 billion (about $2.9 billion), up 68% year on-year. The shift is seen as structural rather than seasonal, with Chiang stating that cloud investment will be the most critical driver over the next few years. The firm also reiterated its full-year guidance of "strong" growth, while highlighting geopolitical volatility as a primary risk.
articles.shortSummary: Foxconn's Q2 2026 net profit surged 35% to a record NT$59.97 billion, driven by strong AI server demand and increased cloud computing revenue.

articles.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has added $100 billion to its Arizona commitment, raising its total US pledge to $265 billion across 12 facilities, marking the largest direct investment from a foreign company in American history. The expansion is not just more factory floor space but also dedicated advanced packaging capacity to Arizona, specifically CoWoS (Chip on Wafer on Substrate), the 2.5D packaging technology used by major AI accelerators. Despite the record results, TSMC's US-listed shares fell more than 2% on the day. The company also reported a record-breaking net income of NT$706.56 billion ($22 billion), a 77.4% increase year-over-year. For Q3 2026, TSMA guided revenue of $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion, with an operating profit margin of 56% to 58%. The company now expects revenue growth slightly above 40% in US dollar terms, up from previous guidance of more than 30%.
articles.shortSummary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company increased its commitment to Arizona to $265 billion, targeting advanced packaging for AI accelerators, despite record quarterly profits and increased capex.

articles.summary: TSMC announced its highest-ever monthly revenue figure, NT$442.68 billion in June, a 67.9% jump from June 2025 and a 6.2% increase from May 2026, the largest in the company's nearly four-decade history. The announcement was delayed due to Typhoon Bavi's disruption to Taiwan's financial markets. The company's consolidated net sales were reported at approximately NT$1.27 trillion, or about $39.6 billion, pushing it past the top of guidance set in April and potentially up against the high end of TSMC's own April guidance of $39 billion to $40.2 billion. Despite this, TSMC is expected to exceed $40 billion in AI-related chip revenue for the full year, accounting for roughly 25% of projected total revenue. The most advanced production process for AI chips, N3, operates on booking cycles that run 12 to 18 months ahead of delivery. The revenue beat could push TSMC’s Q2 gross margin above the 67.1% consensus estimate.
articles.shortSummary: TSMC set an All-time revenue record with a 67.9% rise in June, reflecting rapidly changing AI-driven demand, driven by a typhoon's disruption of seasonal growth patterns.

articles.summary: TSMC has broken ground on additional advanced packaging fabs in the second phase of the Chiayi Science Park in southern Taiwan, according to National Science and Technology Council minister Wu Cheng-wen. The expansion is aimed at increasing demand for high-performance computing chips, particularly in packaging. The National Science & Technology Council Minister stated that three advanced packaging facilities will be added in Phase II, with the site being developed into a packaging cluster led by TSMC. Once completed, companies at the park are expected to generate over NT$300bn ($9.35bn) in annual output and support around 9,000 jobs. The groundbreaking came on the same day TSMC reported record second-quarter revenue of T$1.27tn ($39.62bn), up 36% year on year and slightly ahead of an LSEG SmartEstimate.
articles.shortSummary: TSMC is building three advanced packaging facilities in Chiayi, aiming to meet growing AI demand and support 9,000 jobs.

articles.summary: Nigigio is increasing its research and supply chain resources towards the Feynman AI Platform, a major architectural evolution from the Vera Rubin platform, as it enters mass production and ramp-up. Feynmen is expected to feature 3D chiplets, TSMC’s System on Integrated Chips (SoIC) technology, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and co-packaged optics (CPO), and could push NVLink bandwidth beyond 1,000 terabytes per second as Nvidia builds increasingly large AI clusters. The accelerated roadmap is putting pressure on TSMC to expand advanced packaging capacity. The report also revealed that TSMC is accelerating construction at its AP7 facility in Chiayi and AP8 in the Southern Taiwan Science Park, while preparing capacity for SoIC, CoWoS-L and next-generation CoPoS technologies. Nvidia is scheduled to report its second-quarter results on Aug. 26. The company has also begun working with major financial institutions on an AI infrastructure financing platform targeting more than $500 billion in third-party capital.
articles.shortSummary: Nvidia is rapidly ramping up production for its next-gen Feynman AI platform, pushing TSMC to expand SoIC capacity, boosting revenue forecasts and collaborating with major financial institutions.

articles.title: TSMC is quietly borrowing a page from Intel's playbook
articles.description: The chipmaking rivalry just took an unexpected turn behind the scenes.
articles.content:
Companies rarely name a secret internal project after a rival’s product. Doing so hands over the story before it even becomes public: that the smaller competitor built something worth copying.

That i... [4928 symbols]
articles.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) is reportedly developing a new chip-packaging technology, "EMIB-like," which borrows directly from Intel’s Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge (EMIBB), a technique that often looks unconventional but becomes standard once a competitor wins contracts. The move comes as TSMC, the undisputed leader in advanced packaging, currently packages its most advanced AI chips through Chip-on-Wafer-Substrate (CoWoS), used by customers including Nvidia and AMD. However, this dominance came with lead times stretching to 78 weeks in some cases, leading to a backlog of product sales. Packaging represents only 10% to 15% of TSMC's annual revenue, but this understates the stakes as AI infrastructure spending from cloud hyperscalers is near $700 billion in 2026. If Nvidia adopts Intel‘s packaging for even one product line, it could gain the industry's most important customer.
articles.shortSummary: TSMC is developing "EMIB-like” packaging to compete with Intel's advanced multi-die technology, positioning itself as a potential strategic ally of both companies.

This growth is more structural than coincidental, as AI accelerator chips require simultaneous demand on multiple layers of the supply chain simultaneously. The DRAM sector nearly quadrupled year-over-year in June, while the packaging houses and substrate makers expanded in lockstep with the foundries. TSMC's consolidated revenue of NT$442.68 billion (approximately US$13.8 billion) for the month was reported, an unusual result for a month that had seen sequential declines in each of the prior four years. This comes as the magnitude-7.1 earthquake that hit Japan's Kumamoto Prefecture on July 28 raises uncertainty about when the second facility, targeting 3-nanometer AI chips, will reach production. Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Inc. (JASM), the TSMC-majority-owned joint venture operating the Kumamoto facilities, recorded a net profit of NT$951 million (approximately $29 million USD) in the first quarter of 2026, compared to a loss of NT $1.39 billion (approximately €43 million USD), and a loss $3.25 billion (about $101 million USD)" in the same period a year earlier. The construction site of the second Fab 2 was unaffected and work has resumed following additional safety inspections.

articles.summary: A new analysis from Tech Week reveals that the US cannot finish its own AI chips at home, despite a $265B investment by TSMC and the announcement of dedicated advanced packaging capacity in Arizona. The analysis also revealed that every accelerator built at TSMC's Phoenix fab travels to Taiwan for CoWoS packaging before it can ship. This is a significant policy gap at the center of a global semiconductor race that has seen four different national strategies. The CHIPS Act funding, plus tax credits, has led to an expansion of American silicon fabrication capacity, with the crown jewel being TSMC’s Fab 21 campus outside Phoenix reaching approximately 92% yield on 4nm production. However, demand continues to exceed supply. CoWOS, the 2.5D advanced packaging process that every major AI accelerator on the market depends on, is not a refinement of wafer fabrication. The US has invested $265 billion across 12 planned facilities, the largest foreign direct investment in American history.
articles.shortSummary: Despite TSMC's $265 billion investment, the United States faces a significant gap in advanced packaging, with every AI chip manufactured in Taiwan.

articles.summary: TSMC is reportedly developing a chip packaging technology similar to Intel's Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge (EMIB), or "EMIB Like," which uses silicon bridges to connect multiple chip components, enabling larger, more complex processors while reducing manufacturing costs. If TSMC launches an EMIB-like packaging technology, it could pose a threat to Intel Foundry's dominance. This comes after Intel announced a strategic partnership with China's Lens Technology to develop glass substrate-based advanced semiconductor packaging for future AI and data center chips.
articles.shortSummary: TSMC is developing advanced chip packaging similar to Intel's EMIB, potentially boosting Intel's stock and boosting investor confidence.

articles.summary: The global market for fan-out panel-level packaging (FO-PLP) and glass substrates is set to grow by tenfold in five years, according to Counterpoint Research. The market is expected to expand from $650 million in 2024 to more than $8.1 billion in 2030, with FO-PLPP accounting for 45.6% of revenue. Two physical limits, including geometry and material, are forcing the change. FO-P builds packages on large rectangular panels instead of round silicon wafers, which reduces waste and increases area utilization to 75% and reduces cost. The second limit is material, as packages grow large, causing the substrate beneath them to warp when heated during manufacturing. East Asia is predicted to hold 84.8% of panel-levels packaging capacity by 2030.
articles.shortSummary: The global market for fan-out panel-level packaging, driven by geometry and material, is expected to grow 10x to meet growing AI chip demands.
